title: Two Sum
content:
Problem Statement
Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return the indices of the two numbers such that they add up to target.
You may assume that each input would have exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice.
--------------------------------------------------
Example 1:
Input:
nums = [2,7,11,15]
target = 9
Output:
[0,1]
Explanation:
Because nums[0] + nums[1] == 9, we return [0,1].
--------------------------------------------------
Example 2:
Input:
nums = [3,2,4]
target = 6
Output:
[1,2]
--------------------------------------------------
Example 3:
Input:
nums = [3,3]
target = 6
Output:
[0,1]
--------------------------------------------------
Constraints:
- 2 ≤ nums.length ≤ 10^4
- -10^9 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 10^9
- -10^9 ≤ target ≤ 10^9
- Only one valid answer exists.
--------------------------------------------------
Input Format:
- First line: space-separated integers representing array nums
- Second line: integer target
Output Format:
- Return two space-separated integers representing indices
--------------------------------------------------
Function Signature (JavaScript):
function twoSum(nums, target) {
  // return [index1, index2]
}
--------------------------------------------------
Edge Cases to Consider:
- Negative numbers
- Duplicate values
- Very large arrays
--------------------------------------------------
Follow-up:
Can you come up with an algorithm that is faster than O(n^2) time complexity?
